item.title: R Contrasts Error: Troubleshooting Factors with Single Levels
item.description:
“R Contrasts Error: Troubleshooting Factors with Single Levels”

This pervasive error in R, particularly when using functions like lm() or glm(), arises when a categorical variable (a factor) intended for statistical modeling analysis has only one level (or fewer). This limitation prevents the creation of a contrast matrix, which is essential for estimating model coefficients. The problem is often compounded by data complexities such as missing values (NA), subsetting, or factors with unused levels. Identifying the exact cause can be tricky as the data used for fitting might differ from the initially provided dataset.

item.title: R: Finding the Statistical Mode of Data
item.description:
“R: Finding the Statistical Mode of Data”

Calculating the statistical mode, the value that appears most frequently in a dataset, is a common task in data analysis. While R’s base installation doesn’t have a direct mode() function for statistical purposes (the built-in mode() asserts variable types), numerous methods exist to achieve this. This post explores various approaches, from custom functions to package solutions, catering to different needs like handling multiple modes or NA values.
